why: Legs 1 and 2 hold; leg 3 fails, and the finding's own OUR STATE carries a false half. (1) QUOTE - VERBATIM but TRUNCATED at the load-bearing clause. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop.md` (960 lines), line 722, in the `### Managed settings` table, contains the claimed text as an exact substring. Reading the WHOLE line, two sentences were cut: 'Available in third-party (3P) Desktop deployments only. Deliver this key through the managed settings file or MDM, since third-party deployments do not receive admin-console settings.' The second cut sentence is the one the finding paraphrases into its claim; the FIRST is the one it drops, and it is the scope limit - the key exists only in third-party deployments of Claude Desktop, i.e. Anthropic's own app shipped into a fleet whose deployer is not Anthropic. Nessy is not a Claude Desktop deployment: it is a separate application whose vendor and deployer are the same organization, so the vendor/administrator separation the MDM push channel bridges does not exist here. 'Our fork is precisely the third-party deployment shape the key exists for' is the finding's own inference, not the page's. (2) CITATIONS - ACCURATE. `managed-policy.ts:129-130` are exactly `readonly allowedMcpServers?: readonly ManagedMcpEntryV1[]` / `readonly deniedMcpServers?: readonly ManagedMcpEntryV1[]`; `:501` is `export const MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS = [`, whose 30-key list contains no MCP-server-definition key. The absence is real: `grep -ran managedMcpServers` over the whole tree (with -a) hits only doc/spec files - `2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:698`, the sweep TSV/JSON, and this row. `toolPolicy` appears once in product code, as the type of an unused `RuntimeMcpServer.toolPolicy` field (`capabilities/resolver.ts:316`, interface at `:133`), with no producer or consumer. (3) CONSEQUENCE - HALF FALSE. OUR STATE asserts the managed policy 'carries no per-server tool restriction'. It does. The same admin-only file the MCP lists arrive in - `/Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json`, `/etc/nessy/managed-policy.json`, `%ProgramData%\Nessy\managed-policy.json` (`server-core/src/pi-harness/managed-policy-loader.ts:48-50`), plus a `managed-policy.d/` drop-in dir - carries `permissionDsl` (`managed-policy.ts:82`, key at `:504`) and `claudeRules`, and that DSL has a first-class `mcp` matcher: `permission-dsl.ts:946-950` splits a tool's `permissionName` on `__` and wildcard-matches SERVER and TOOL independently, so `mcp__jira__delete_*` is exactly 'restrict which tools in that server users can invoke'. `claude-permission-rules.ts:171` parses the `mcp__server__tool` spelling from managed `claudeRules` too. It is enforced, not parsed-and-dropped: `SessionManager.ts:4095-4096` passes `managedPermissionDsl` into the turn, `:14267`/`:16245` read it again, the shipped docblock at `managed-policy.ts:299-301` names it as THE admin boundary ('a managed `permissionDsl` deny rule, which our deterministic gate applies BEFORE the judge is consulted at all'), and `isWholeToolDenyForIdentity` additionally REMOVES a wholly-denied MCP tool from the model's context. So the per-server tool-restriction half of the divergence is simply not a gap. (4) The remaining half - no managed key that PUSHES a server definition - is true, but it is (a) already recorded, not undiscovered, and (b) met differently by this fork's deployment shape. Recorded: `docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:91` files the `managed-mcp.json` fixed deployment as 'documented, not implemented - a separate deployment channel', and the sibling finding f039, on that same absence, was already refuted 2026-08-02. Met differently: the fork ships the corporate server set IN THE PRODUCT - `BUILTIN_DP_MCP_SERVERS` (`packages/shared/src/mcp/builtin-dp-servers.ts:111`) is 29 frozen `dp ai mcp` server definitions (dpGitlab, dpJira, dpSage, SpiritK8s, ...) delivered to every user of the deployment, each with a `defaultEnabled` and a per-server user toggle (`config/builtin-dp-mcp-settings.ts`, `builtin-dp-mcp-preferences.ts`). 'Every user in this deployment gets these servers' is answered at build time because there is one organization, one gateway and one builder - which is the same de-brand/corporate-target difference that removes the admin console, the claude.ai connectors and the MDM fleet from this product. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in `2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` section 3 - I read all nine; none concerns MCP deployment.
correctedState: Verbatim quote, but truncated before the clause that scopes it: `managedMcpServers` is 'Available in third-party (3P) Desktop deployments only' - third-party fleet deployments of Anthropic's Claude Desktop, where deployer and vendor differ. Nessy is not such a deployment; it is built and shipped by the organization that runs it. Of the two things the finding says we lack, one is false and one is a recorded, differently-met absence. FALSE: 'carries no per-server tool restriction'. The same admin-only `managed-policy.json` (system paths at `managed-policy-loader.ts:48-50`, plus `managed-policy.d/`) carries `permissionDsl`/`claudeRules`, whose `mcp` matcher wildcard-matches server and tool separately (`permission-dsl.ts:946-950`, `claude-permission-rules.ts:171`), is applied by the deterministic gate before any judge (`managed-policy.ts:299-301`, `SessionManager.ts:4095`), and strips a wholly-denied MCP tool from context - i.e. an administrator can already restrict which tools of a named server users may invoke. TRUE but not new: no managed key pushes a server DEFINITION. That absence is the `managed-mcp.json` deployment channel already recorded at `docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:91` as 'documented, not implemented - a separate deployment channel' (sibling finding f039 refuted on it). This fork meets the need at build time instead: `BUILTIN_DP_MCP_SERVERS` (`mcp/builtin-dp-servers.ts:111`) ships 29 corporate dp MCP servers to every user with per-server defaults and toggles. If a real gap is ever filed here it should be narrow: an admin-authored server SET in the managed file, not a claim about tool policy.
